home.title: Learn Docker and DevOps from scratch
home.intro: No prior knowledge needed. Every new word is explained before it is used, and every lesson ends with hands-on missions that the site checks for you.

fromZero.title: Truly from zero
fromZero.text: We start with what an operating system is and how to use the terminal, then move on to Docker, pipelines and production.

missions.title: Checked missions
missions.text: Quizzes, a simulated terminal, files to write and labs on real Docker. Every answer gets feedback explaining what works and what is missing.

local.title: Your progress stays yours
local.text: No account and no server: everything is saved only in this browser. You can export your progress to a file and pick it up elsewhere.

map.title: Course map
map.intro: The course is divided into worlds. Each world contains levels to complete in order and ends with a final challenge.

perseverante.name: Persistent
perseverante.description: Pass a mission after at least 5 attempts: making mistakes is part of learning.

serie-7.name: Week on fire
serie-7.description: Study for 7 days in a row.

backup.title: Saving your progress
backup.intro: Progress is saved only in this browser. Export it to a file to keep a backup or to continue on another device.

backup.confirmImport: The file contains {{lessons}} lessons read and {{missions}} missions passed. Replace your current progress with it?
backup.confirmReset: All progress, XP and badges will be deleted from this browser. This cannot be undone.

gym.title: Terminal gym
gym.intro: A free terminal where you can try commands without fear of breaking anything: it's a simulated computer that lives only on this page. Linux and Docker are included.
gym.note: The simulator reproduces the behavior and messages of real commands, in a reduced version. When a command isn't available, it tells you.

hints.unknownCommand: The command “{{command}}” doesn't exist or the course simulator doesn't know it. Check the spelling, or type help to see the available commands.
hints.interactiveShell: Here a shell would open inside the container, waiting for your commands. The simulator doesn't reproduce interactive sessions: the container is closed right away.
hints.foregroundStopped: The container “{{name}}” was running in the foreground: in real life the terminal would stay busy until you press Ctrl+C. The simulator pressed it for you and the container stopped. To keep it running in the background use the -d option.
hints.notSimulated: “{{command}}” exists in Docker, but it isn't available in the course simulator yet.
hints.execLimited: In the simulator this command doesn't keep running inside the container.
hints.helpIntro: Welcome to the simulated terminal! Type a command and press Enter. Type help to see the available commands; type command-name --help to learn how to use it (for example: ls --help).
hints.helpFooter: The simulator reproduces real commands in a reduced version: for all the options check the official documentation.
hints.manReduced: This is a reduced version of the {{command}} manual. The full one is on man7.org.
